channel.title: OpenSSF Glossary – Gemara
channel.description: Recent content in Gemara on OpenSSF Glossary

item.title: : Assessment
item.description:
(1) the process of determining whether an outcome meets the actor’s intent; or (2) an atomic process within an Evaluation used to determine a resource’s Compliance with an Assessment Requirement.

Source: Gemara

Industry Cross-Reference

An assessment is the testing and/or evaluation of the management, operational, and technical security controls to determine the extent to which the controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended, and producing the desired outcome with respect to meeting the security requirements for an information system or organization.

Source: NIST CSRC Glossary - Assessment

item.title: : Assessment Requirement
item.description:
A tightly scoped, verifiable condition that must be satisfied and confirmed by an evaluator.

Source: Gemara

Industry Cross-Reference

Industry Equivalent: Assessment Objective

An assessment requirement (or assessment objective) is a set of determination statements related to a security control that dictates what must be evaluated to ensure compliance and effectiveness.

Source: NIST CSRC Glossary - Assessment Objective

item.title: : Catalog
item.description:
A structured set of related prose and relevant metadata.

Source: Gemara

Industry Cross-Reference

Industry Equivalent: Catalog

The collection of all assessment elements.

Source: NIST CSRC Glossary - Catalog

item.title: : Compliance
item.description:
Adherence to a Rule or set of Rules.

Source: Gemara

Industry Cross-Reference

Compliance is the adherence to, and the ability to demonstrate adherence to, mandated requirements defined by laws, regulations, and organizational standards.

Source: ISACA Glossary - Compliance

item.title: : Continuous Monitoring
item.description:
A multi-system process designed to collect Evaluation and operational data on an ongoing basis to better detect malicious action and non-compliance, enable Remediative Enforcement, and observe trends over time.

Source: Gemara

Industry Cross-Reference

Continuous monitoring is the process of maintaining ongoing awareness of information security, vulnerabilities, and threats to support organizational risk management decisions.

Source: NIST CSRC Glossary - Continuous Monitoring

item.title: : Governance
item.description:
Strategic oversight of an organization and its activities.

Source: Gemara

Industry Cross-Reference

Industry Equivalent: Risk Governance

The process by which risk management evaluation, decisions, and actions are connected to enterprise strategy and objectives. Risk governance provides the transparency, responsibility, and accountability that enables managers to acceptably manage risk.

Source: NIST CSRC Glossary - Risk Governance

item.title: : Guidance
item.description:
Prose intended to help bring about a desired outcome for a topic or generalized scenario, based on knowledge of relevant Vectors.

Source: Gemara

item.title: : Guideline
item.description:
Atomic element of a Guidance Catalog; often includes explanatory context and recommendations for designing optimal implementations.

Source: Gemara

Industry Cross-Reference

A guideline is a statement used to provide additional explanatory information for a specific rule, standard, or control, often recommending a specific approach to implementation without being strictly mandatory.

Source: ISACA Glossary - Guideline

item.title: : Intent Evaluation
item.description:
An Evaluation ensuring that a resource is prepared in alignment with Policy, such as through proper training, configuration, or code.

Source: Gemara

item.title: : Objective
item.description:
A unified statement of intent, which may encompass multiple situationally applicable statements or requirements.

Source: Gemara

Industry Cross-Reference

Industry Equivalent: Objective

A statement of a desired outcome.

Source: ISACA Glossary - Objective

item.title: : Organization
item.description:
Any logical grouping of human, physical, virtual, and information resources such as a company, business unit, or team.

Source: Gemara

Industry Cross-Reference

An organization is an entity of any size, complexity, or positioning within an organizational structure (e.g., a federal agency, a private company, or any of its operational elements) that defines and operates its own governance structure.

Source: NIST CSRC Glossary - Organization

item.title: : Policy
item.description:
A clearly-scoped set of rules based on an organization’s Risk Appetite.

Source: Gemara

Industry Cross-Reference

A policy is a set of statements, rules, or assertions, formulated and enforced by the governing body of an organization, to direct and limit its actions in pursuit of long-term goals and specify expected behaviors.

Source: NIST CSRC Glossary - Policy

item.title: : Preventive Enforcement
item.description:
Any action that interrupts another process which would otherwise cause non-compliance.

Source: Gemara

Industry Cross-Reference

Industry Equivalent: Preventive Control

An internal control that is used to avoid undesirable events, errors and other occurrences that an enterprise has determined could have a negative material effect on a process or end product.

Source: ISACA Glossary - Preventive Control

item.title: : Remediative Enforcement
item.description:
Corrective action in response to non-compliance in a deployed activity.

Source: Gemara

Industry Cross-Reference

Industry Equivalent: Corrective Control

A control designed to correct errors, omissions, unauthorized uses and intrusions, once they are detected.

Source: ISACA Glossary - Corrective Control

item.title: : Residual Risk
item.description:
The Risk remaining after Risk Mitigation and Enforcement actions have been implemented.

Source: Gemara

Industry Cross-Reference

Industry Equivalent: Actual Residual Risk

Residual risk is the risk that remains after management has taken action to alter its severity, such as implementing mitigating security controls or remediation efforts.

Source: NIST CSRC Glossary - Actual Residual Risk

item.title: : Risk Acceptance
item.description:
A clearly documented decision to accept an unmitigated Risk as necessary or unavoidable.

Source: Gemara

Industry Cross-Reference

Risk acceptance is a formal, documented decision to accept the identified risk and monitor it periodically, usually because the cost of mitigation outweighs the potential loss or the risk falls within accepted thresholds.

Source: ISACA Glossary - Risk Acceptance

item.title: : Risk Appetite
item.description:
The level of Risk an organization is willing to accept in pursuit of its objectives.

Source: Gemara

Industry Cross-Reference

Risk appetite is the types and broad-based amount of risk an organization is willing to accept in its pursuit of value or mission/vision.

Source: NIST CSRC Glossary - Risk Appetite

item.title: : Risk Assessment
item.description:
The process of identifying the potential or actual Risks introduced by a system.

Source: Gemara

Industry Cross-Reference

Risk assessment is the process of identifying, estimating, and prioritizing risks to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, reputation), assets, and individuals resulting from the operation of an information system.

Source: NIST CSRC Glossary - Risk Assessment

item.title: : Risk Catalog
item.description:
A group of related Risks relevant to an organization; used to determine when and how Policies are created for the organization.

Source: Gemara

Industry Cross-Reference

Industry Equivalent: Risk Register

A list of risk scenarios that have been identified, analyzed and prioritized.

Source: ISACA Glossary - Risk Register

item.title: : Rule
item.description:
An active, enforceable Policy, regulation, or law.

Source: Gemara

Industry Cross-Reference

A rule is an explicitly stated principle, regulation, or authorization condition governing conduct, action, or procedure within an information system or organizational policy framework.

Source: NIST CSRC Glossary - Rule

item.title: : Sensitive Activity
item.description:
A type of action that introduces Risk to an organization.

Source: Gemara
